newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE FIGHTS RED LOCUST SWARMS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE FIGHTS RED LOCUST SWARMS.

text.p: Zimbabwean farmers are trying to eradicate swarms of red locusts in parts of the country before the start of the planting season next month, an agriculture official said on Sunday.

"The fight is still on...but we hope we will be on top of the situation by the end of this month. We just have to, and we are moving very hard to do that," Di Taylor, an entomologist with the main Commercial Farmers Union (CFU), told Reuters.

As well as ground spraying, commercial farmers and the state Agricultural Extension Services (Agritex) have deployed planes to spray the locusts, which hit mainly the eastern and southern districts in August after the end of the 1995/96 (November- April) cropping season, she said.
According to the CFU's weekly Farmer Magazine published on Friday, crop damage has so far been minimal and confined mostly to winter irrigated crops, grass and tree leaves.

The red locust swarms came in from neighbouring Mozambique, and Taylor said Agritex and the CFU were still trying to determine their spread. She said it was not yet clear if there was a danger of swarms moving into South Africa.
